title: Rationale for New Pre-Court Action Protocol for Business-to-Business Debt Claims
what_it_is: Rationale for New Pre-Court Action Protocol for Business-to-Business Debt Claims

sections.label: New Pre-Court Action Protocol
sections.summary: The new Pre-Court Action Protocol for Business-to-Business Debt Claims is an initiative by the State Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Speaker, the new Pre-Court Action Protocol for Business-to-Business Debt Claims is an initiative by the State Courts.

sections.label: Protocol scope and case numbers
sections.summary: The Protocol applies to all business-to-business debt claims commenced in the State Courts from 1 October 2019, about 1,000 yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new Protocol applies to all business-to-business debt claims that are commenced in the State Courts from 1 October 2019 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The State Courts see about 1,000 business-to-business debt claims each year.

sections.label: Cost sanctions for non-compliance
sections.summary: The Court may impose cost sanctions on a non-compliant party, creditor or debtor, if no good reasons are shown.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Court has the discretion to impose cost sanctions on a party who does not comply with the new Protocol, whether the creditor or debtor, if the defaulting party is unable to show good reasons for the non-compliance.

sections.label: Factors for cost sanctions
sections.summary: Various factors apply when the Court assesses cost sanctions for non-compliance, and a creditor may proceed without 28 days' notice in some cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There are a variety of factors which come into play when the Court assesses ultimately whether there should be cost sanctions against one or the other party should there be non-compliance with the Protocol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if the creditor forms the assessment that this debtor has been dragging his feet or is facing a series of claims which might cause the debtor to go into bankruptcy, thereby, triggering a series of other consequences, then, on those cases, the creditor may proceed, even without 28 days' notice.

sections.label: 28 days and case resolution
sections.summary: 28 days is usually shorter than Court engagement, 75% of the thousand cases resolve without Court, and the 28 days is not fixed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In most cases, as Mr Lim Biow Chuan would be aware, 28 days would probably be far shorter than if the matter had to be engaged in Court altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And bearing in mind that 75% of the thousand cases end up in some form or another resolved without having gone to Court, the State Court's Protocol seeks to try to address the vast majority of these cases with upfront information, with details to facilitate as far as possible the parties' resolution by themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But as I had mentioned, and I would like to go back to it, the 28 days is not written in stone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And if the party is able to justify a departure from it, the Court will consider that and not impose sanctions.
